so: the positive cannot be run today at all. It is blocked on acquisition, not on implementation and not on a choice to defer it - there is no period in this repository that both has its original and is shard-resident.
the_open_item: A complete end-to-end positive for a target year whose 10-K row lives in a submissions history shard rather than in filings.recent. It has been on the list since historical_metadata_context was written, with Marriott 2023 recorded as a non-latest-year positive that does not replace it.

what_is_covered_and_what_is_not.covered: historical_metadata_context's shard-reading path has unit coverage over three shard-resident company periods, which parse and name their source shard.
what_is_covered_and_what_is_not.not_covered: no Run has ever been created for a shard-resident period, so the path from that metadata view through installation, native Run, freeze, cold read and public row is untested end to end.
what_is_covered_and_what_is_not.why_that_distinction_matters: the unit coverage says the view resolves. It says nothing about whether everything downstream of it handles a period selected from a shard, and this repository's own history is a series of things that only failed once they were wired together.

what_was_measured: for each of the eleven target periods whose original is saved, which inventory block its 10-K row came from - read from the row's own metadata_origin rather than inferred from 'the latest filing is always in recent'.

what_would_unblock_it.cheapest: Salesforce 2023-01-31 and 2022-01-31, whose 10-K rows are shard-resident and whose originals are class A of the acquisition plan.
